utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning. May we begin by taking the appearances today, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Tom Hannis and Crispian Smith on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing finish Stanisic Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic and Eric Tully for the Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. There being no preliminary matters, could we have the witness returned to the stand, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: While he's coming in, Your Honours, I just wanted to advise you, the only thing I propose to do with him further on direct is to ask him a couple of questions and then tender -- I propose to tender two documents, they're both Assembly sessions of the RS National Assembly, one is from November 23rd and 24th, 1992; and the other one is from -- it's a portion from September 1993. But that one is a retrospective where there are discussions about what happened in 1992 and I think it's relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And although this witness speaks at both Assembly sessions, I want Your Honours to see the entire Assembly session. I think it's the only way you can make sense out of it. If I try to give you just two pages or five pages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, one of them is 566 pages. And the first one, I'm not sure, is much shorter. It's only 123 in English. But if Your Honours will be patient --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We appreciate the idea of context, Mr. Hannis, but if we're going to get such a large chunk, it may be useful to indicate by highlighting or some other means what -- where to put in the context of the entire session the bit on which you're relying.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, I will -- what I thought of doing with this witness was just to have him read a couple of paragraphs that are of particular interest to me at this point this morning. I'll tender the documents, and I certainly would be willing to highlight before the end of our case those portions that we think are most pertinent to you. But again, I guess I'll save that argument for later on, and maybe I can persuade you further, but if not we'll certainly highlight what we think is important, and the Defence, I'm sure, will highlight what they think is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Doctor. Welcome back. I wanted to ask you, during 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Let me remind him that he's still on his oath. Good morning, Dr. Djokanovic. Yes, please continue, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Doctor, in 1992 and 1993 by virtue of the positions you held, did you have occasion to regularly attend the sessions of the National Assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended almost every session, perhaps I missed one, two, or three.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I would like to show you now exhibit -- it's 65 ter number 933. First we'll bring up the cover page, and I would indicate, Doctor, that this is a tape-recording or the transcript of the 22nd Session of the RS National Assembly held on two days, the 23rd and the 24th of November. Do you recall attending this session?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That session was held in Zvornik. I attended it, and I also made some remarks at the session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 107 of the English and 103 of the B/C/S. Doctor, I hope these pages are what I think they are, and it should show you as a speaker. And you're talking about the work of the war commissioners. Do you recall addressing that subject during this session?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was toward the end of the session, where I spoke, and there was a lot negative said on the day before regarding this issue. So then I took occasion to say a few words about the function of the war commissioners and that the main task was to introduce the civilian authorities, practically to establish the state in the field, as it were, and to also introduce by name the people who would be responsible for things happening at that time and also for the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you recall this being the session where the resignation of Prime Minister Djeric was discussed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This was the session where Prime Minister Djeric submitted his resignation, although this entire matter was a bit disputable. He really wanted the deputies to actually cast a vote of confidence on his role, but he actually tripped on this because the Assemblymen did not -- they refused to vote. They just accepted his resignation. However, he was given until the end of that session to actually withdraw his resignation, which he didn't do, so that at that session his resignation was actually adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And I would now like to go to page 21 of the English and page 17 of the B/C/S. And, Doctor, in a moment I'm going to ask you to read from the B/C/S for us because I want to be sure that my English translation is as accurate as possible. And I will tell you that the speaker in this section is Mr. Mico Stanisic, and he's addressing some remarks that had been made by and concerning the prime minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in the English, Your Honours, we're going to start from about eight or nine lines up from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And for you, Doctor, if you could from the bottom of the B/C/S page go up about 11 lines. There's a sentence that in B/C/S begins with the words [Interpretation] "For that reason we therefore ..." [In English] You find it, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If it would assist, Your Honours, I can hand him a hard copy of the portion I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't really make out all the letters. Some of them are darker and some are less. So if you can perhaps just blow it up a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Or perhaps the usher can give you my hard copy, and I think maybe it's easier to read. Could you read the portion that's been highlighted there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Therefore, we insisted that no one can just say, "You're not doing a good job because I feel that you're Radovan's man. That is no argument for me. I would like - and we tried to do because we had reservists in the police at the beginning - we wanted them to defend the country. We took on board thieves and criminals, and we even had a Ph.D. who held a gun in his hand. And he did not come out to defend his country nor any other intellectual, but our priority task was we had the best of intentions, But perhaps we made a mistake there. Maybe I made a mistake, too, I allow that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, based on that reading, I see some differences between what was just translated and what's in the English translation. I will submit this portion of the document for a revised or final translation from CLSS. But I would like to tender Exhibit 933.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P400, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Doctor, one last document is 65 ter number 3399. And this is part of a session, I believe it's the 34th Session, during 1993 which extended over something like five or six days on three different -- at three different locations. Do you recall attending this session of the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this session of the Assembly. It started at the end of August and ended toward the end of September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 277 of the English, and I believe it's 320 in the B/C/S. What post did you hold at this time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this time I was the minister of veteran's affairs in the Government of Republika Srpska. The entire -- the full name was the Ministry for Issues Relating to War Veterans and Victims of the War.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you should see now on your screen that the page where you are shown to be a speaker, and in my English the very first line you seem to be calling on your legislative immunity, in that you're reminding everybody of your protection when you're speaking in the Assembly from being arrested or punished for expressing your opinion. Can you tell us briefly why you did that and what you were discussing in the session at this point.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the time when a unit of the Republika Srpska army in Banja Luka took over power, and we - when I say "we," I mean members of the government and the deputies and of course members of the Presidency as well as the top brass of the army - they informed us that there was fighting in Banja Luka, that there was destruction, and that this was practically an assault on Republika Srpska. On this session Radovan Karadzic ordered Ratko Mladic, and he was supported by almost all of the deputies, he was also supported by a member of the Presidency, Mrs. Biljana Plavsic, to resolve this military situation in Banja Luka. Practically he ordered Ratko Mladic to use the army to quell this rebellion. I recalled my immunity as a member of the government and warned Radovan Karadzic that he should not do that, that he should not push Ratko Mladic, as it were, into a conflict with a portion of his own army. Of course this entire session was practically a plot by Radovan Karadzic to actually settle accounts with a new government and also with the top personalities. I warned Mr. Karadzic explicitly that he should not do that, that these were special conditions, wartime conditions, that this republic was not his fiefdom, and that the Serb people and all its politicians and members of government were part of it. Of course after this he launched an attack on me -- or rather, a number of deputies stood up and spoke against me. And at this session the then-president of the Executive Board of the SDS and a deputy from Zvornik, Jovo Mijatovic, he harangued against me, and he actually misquoted me. He misquoted something that I had said in June in Zvornik. Jovo Mijatovic then said, "Mr. Dragan Djokanovic said in Zvornik that Brano Grujic and the municipal leadership of Zvornik would be accused of genocide." He actually turned my words around. I said at the time, "You might be called on or accused of genocide," and I -- it was by way of warning. But in this conflict with me he said that Dragan Djokanovic had said that they would be charged with genocide. Of course, after this -- these comments of his, I spoke again and I replied in response to what he said and also the vice-president of the Assembly, Branko Simic, and the president of the republic, Radovan Karadzic, because the three of them had actually launched this attack on me. And I explained that the worst that Jovo Mijatovic quoted, that actually what I had done was warn them about the possibility of being charged of genocide, that I didn't actually say that they would be charged, and I also stated that there had been no genocide in Zvornik, that the Serbian people is not prone to -- not genocidal in its character, and that it never wanted an ethnically clean territory, but that some day it will be discovered who were the perpetrators of that programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And this entire session, is it fair to say that there was a lot of discussion about what had happened in 1992 and who was responsible for some of the events in 1992, even though this is in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This session of the Assembly as well as the one of November 1992 was an occasion where war crimes could be discussed; however, both these opportunities were lost. And in this Assembly session in Zvornik, one deputy said even, "Had we listened to you, we wouldn't have turned Prijedor into a Serbian city. Had we listened to you, Radovan Karadzic and the leadership." And this was his way of saying that he was completely independent in that respect. In the Assembly session, in the hall where the Assembly was held, everybody stood up applauded. Now, when this issue was opened of possible charges for genocide, members of the Presidency and the deputies just remained quiet and failed to actually take part in this discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's another portion at page 274 of the English, and I think it would be 317 of the B/C/S, that I would just like to bring to your attention. It relates to some discussion by Mr. -- Dr. Karadzic about having asked Mr. Stanisic to create a particular secret service, if you will, and I think that's relevant to some testimony heard last week from the videolink witness. And with that I would like to tender Exhibit 3399, and I will highlight those portions that the Prosecution feels are relevant and probative to the issues in this case. And with that, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P401, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djokanovic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I assume you know I am attorney Cvijetic, and I'm the co-Defence counsel in the team of Mr. Stanisic. I studied a lot that has to do with you, with your political work from 1990, 1991, 1992, all your statements, articles in the newspaper, I looked at the web site of your party, testimony in the Krajisnik case, and also the things you told the Prosecutor's office. I saw that in the period that I referred to, 1990, 1991, and 1992, you had quite a substantial period of political activity. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, events kept overtaking one another with great speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You attended in that period all the key meetings and gatherings --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: There's a lot of background noise going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... regardless of their nature, public large rallies, political rallies, and political meetings that were in an inner circle, circle of the chosen. You were also at some meetings in front of the stage and also behind the stage, behind the scenes. I believe that if -- perhaps you were not the best-informed person about the events, you are certainly a very well-informed person about those events. Would I be correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that I was very well informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. That is why I put the question to you like that. Before I put a specific question to you, can you just tell me this: What do you think, how did you manage to secure access in order to attend these important meetings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1990 I was the first one to appear on the Bosnia-Herzegovina political scene as somebody who wanted to introduce democratic changes in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but I did appear as an exclusively Serbian politician - this was in early May 1990 when I registered the party - and Dr. Karadzic appeared in 1990 but two months later. Those two months, from the time that I appeared until Karadzic appeared, I was very busy to secure permits, to be able to register the Serbian national party because there was a problem at the time in the law in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This was not permitted, the legal -- the Assembly of citizens on an ethnic national basis was forbidden. So when the attempts were made to legalise the party, I supported the establishment of the Serbian Democratic Party of Dr. Radovan Karadzic, and then this work --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you a little bit, and perhaps I can give you a cue so that we can help for a joint explanation. This political party of this democratic federalist party which was in favour of the continuation of the Yugoslav Federation with its remaining four members, was that political platform something that drew all the other political subjects to enable you access for you to be able to attend such important meetings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The democratic party of federalists was registered in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and in its first programme objectives it was in favour of the constituting of a multi-party federal parliament, the democratisation of the federal Yugoslavia, and our party's desire was for this socialist federation to transform into a democratic federation. Of course we wanted it to be a six-member federation, and if this was not possible we were willing to accept whatever was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And this concept was accepted by the Serbian Democratic Party and the socialist party of the Republic of Serbia, and if I'm not mistaken at one point of time it was accepted by Mr. Izetbegovic, too, at a meeting which you attended too, in Sarajevo when he was offered the option of being the first president of this four-member federation and one of the founders of his party to be the president of the council. However, you said that he actually withdrew that acceptance of his actually during the day, later on, or actually in the early evening -- well, you talked about that and you testified.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Izetbegovic accepted the concept of a federal Yugoslavia in mid-February, and the offer for him to be the president of this truncated Yugoslavia was in October 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, this is something that he then later rejected.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was exposed to a lot of pressure so he couldn't really follow-up on what he was up supporting for.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, there was also the Cutileiro Plan, which he accepted, and then after being exposed to pressure he withdrew from the plan.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Lisbon, Dr. Izetbegovic accepted Cutileiro's plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Had he stuck to the plan, according to you, you asserted that there would have been no war in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still believe that if Izetbegovic had adhered firmly to implementation of the Cutileiro Plan, Bosnia-Herzegovina would have remained peaceful.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And probably there would have been no court, and we would not have met here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had there been no war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, then there would have been no people from Bosnia-Herzegovina in this court or before this court.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Djokanovic, I'm not going to dwell on this political aspect of it anymore. I'm going to tell you something else now. Zvornik is a municipality which in the geographical sense can be characterised as the doorway or the place of access into Bosnia and Herzegovina. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Zvornik is a town that you're emotionally tied to and you worked as a doctor there, if I'm not mistaken, on the basis of your CV?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I worked in Zvornik as a young doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: However, Zvornik has a specific characteristic, it has a government. It doesn't have a classical Executive Council of the Municipal Assembly, but it has a Crisis Staff but it also has a government, and this is where it's different from other municipalities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Zvornik Crisis Staff was called the provisional government --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, may we have a date for this proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, do you know when Zvornik got this government?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you were talking about the Crisis Staff in Zvornik, I assume that you're thinking about the beginning of the war. The Zvornik Crisis Staff was called the provisional government.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And that government had its president, did it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government had its president, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And the Zvornik government issued its Official Gazette or some sort of bulletin - I don't know the exact name - in which they published their local regulations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did have a rounded-off legislature.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: What does that mean? Can you explain in a couple of sentences.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that they were completely autonomous in adopting all of their decisions. At the top of this authority there was the provisional government of the municipality of Zvornik. And above them, up until the time that I came to Zvornik and the formation of the war commission, there was no one above that government.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The Zvornik government also had its commander of the Territorial Defence staff, which commanded over the military as well as the paramilitary formations in Zvornik; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zvornik did have a secretary for people's defence. I don't know whom he was in command of.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We're going to prove this with other witnesses, and I think we already did that, but at least we would agree about who it was - this was Mr. Marko Pavlovic, was it not? - and at the time even they didn't know what his real name was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was such suspicions about Marko Pavlovic, and that Marko Pavlovic was not his real name.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Are you aware that this local government -- or the government, actually, didn't consider itself a local government. It considered itself as a government in a kind of city state, if you would agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they felt that they were a mini-state.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: That local government also called and financed - and we presented evidence on this - the paramilitaries to come to this area. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember a municipal session where this was discussed, where the Presidency member Biljana Plavsic stated that she had sent a dispatch to Seselj, Arkan, and Jovic, and called upon all other Serbs outside of that area of ours to come and to fight for Serbdom. In June I didn't form the impression or I didn't know that the municipal leadership or that that temporary government in Zvornik was in any kind of connection with those paramilitary groups that had come to the municipality area, and I didn't know particularly that there was some kind of financial arrangement there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did you find out anything about that later? We have evidence that I can show you, but I'm asking you if you found out anything about that later.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a few years I did find out and I read about how they had actually provided money to those paramilitary groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I wanted to hear that from you because then I don't have to bring in evidence that I had already presented before. This is why I'm doing this. Mr. Djokanovic, you noticed another problem there. You noticed that the local police station and the local chief of the police station were not functioning, were not doing their work. Are you aware that up until the time that you arrived, all the police chiefs and the commanders were appointed either by the local government or by the Crisis Staff. To tell you the truth, I'm not even sure myself how to call them. Did you establish that fact?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They appointed all the commanders at the police station, the chief of the police also, they even appointed the commander of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: However, the first time you came you heard that there were other ugly things going on in Zvornik. That first time when you came, like you said, you didn't have any specific information about what this was, but you noticed that the town was empty, that the civilian population was leaving town, and you saw that something was not quite right. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. It's just that I wouldn't agree about it being something; it was evident what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. What I'm interested in now is how you explain the fact - I'm not going to draw anything from what you said, I want to hear that from you - how do you explain the fact that information about this was not reaching Pale or you as an exceptionally well-informed person, but that you had to see these things only by personally going there. And if I'm not mistaken, you also proposed that commissioners be in communication with the areas in the field. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until -- when I came to Pale, Dr. Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object to the portion of the question regarding -- at line 18 "how do you explain the fact that information about this was not reaching Pale ..." That assumes facts in evidence that are not in evidence, and it calls for speculation by this witness. He would not know whether or not the information may have been reaching others in Pale, such as Dr. Karadzic or Mr. Stanisic; he only knows it wasn't reaching him. He can't speak to that. So I would ask the question to be reformulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that the witness understood my question like that, how was it that he didn't get this information in Pale but had to find this out by personally going to Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Karadzic informed me in Pale that people from outside were not coming to Pale and that he didn't have information about what was happening out in the field. I would like to actually say a few things. Some things need to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Just slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I'm talking about the field, I'm talking about Republika Srpska. When we refer to "the field," we meant the entire Republika Srpska; however, de facto we're talking about the area that is east of Brcko here, the area that the government or that the Presidency of Republika Srpska in that period of 1992 was attempting to establish control over. This is the territory of today's eastern Republika Srpska. The western part of Republika Srpska, west of Brcko, was practically outside of the reach of government or the Presidency in Pale; and for the sake of truth, it has to be said that the deputies from the western area of Republika Srpska did attend Assembly sessions regularly, and probably there was communication or an agreement from before about the cooperation of municipal organs of the Serbian Democratic Party with President Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: When you say "western part," we need to say that this is the Republic of the Serbian Krajina, when you're talking about the western part.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm thinking about the Autonomous Region of the Krajina, the ARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. I apologise. Okay, so you are going to Brcko, you went to Brcko personally. On the basis of information -- I'm sorry, what I mean to say is Zvornik. On the basis of information that you reached -- that you were given that the local authorities were not cooperating with the central authority and you are giving an idea to President Karadzic to establish this kind of communication by means of commissioners. Is that the main purpose of these commissioners' offices?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the decision to form the War Presidency, this decision actually was not implemented at all because he didn't have the option of establishing communications with the local authorities, and they didn't show any desire to cooperate with the Presidency in Pale. I saw what the problem was, and I said that it was necessary to have a man or people who would go out in the field from the Presidency, then these commissioners would find deputies, they would organise a constitutive session of the Municipal Assembly, which would in turn elect an Executive Board and the president of the municipality or confirm the term of office of the previous pre-war president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps we'll re-visit this visit on War Presidencies at the end of this examination, but I would now like to follow things chronologically. For the purpose of shedding some light on the situation in Zvornik, you initiated a very important meeting that was held in early July 1992 in Zvornik where all the commissioners of the region attended - and I believe that you were in charge of this region - and you also ensured that Mr. Karadzic was present as well as Commander Mladic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a meeting of all the persons named as you named them, but this was toward the end of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, I do allow for the possibility of making a mistake by a day or so. However, this was an occasion where the state leadership was able to find for themselves in the field what the situation there was. However, you claim that this meeting was mined -- or undermined by Mr. Pavlovic when he took the floor, and then he discussed topics that weren't really important or matters of priority, whereby he actually squandered the time that Mr. Karadzic and Mladic had, and they had to leave. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. He was just basically trying to somehow use up the time of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, you also attacked him at this meeting and -- but the meeting did not -- was not successful and did not proceed the way that you had envisaged; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was not very successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, you remained in Zvornik and then you were able to learn some more specific information as to what was going on there, and you concluded, among other things, that the local chief of the police station was not actually doing his job properly and that this was not a good personnel decision. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on these several visits to Zvornik, I was able to observe certain matters, and then if the local officials who are there all the time provide information that is contrary to that, that would point to their being incompetent. And the only chance here was for someone to come from Pale - and I mean a member of the Presidency or someone from the police - that they should find a good man to go to Zvornik and who could then observe and note what was happening there and inform the president and the government thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, please slow down. I have to tell you, we speak the same language, and if we speak too fast, then the translation will not be well done. All right, let's go back to this. So you went back to Pale, informed Mr. Karadzic that the problem, among other things, was also in how the local police station was operating. And he then told you to discuss this with Mr. Stanisic and seek for -- and seek a solution; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You then went to see Mr. Stanisic, and if I'm not mistaken you went there together with Professor Koljevic. And you said that Mr. Stanisic listened very carefully to you -- to what you had to say and that he pointed out to you that even at the ministry where he was positioned in Pale itself he did not have sufficient staff or personnel to fill all the positions, but he did promise that he would try and find the right solution for Zvornik, the right choice; but also stating that this will be very difficult, especially if he tried to find someone from outside the area who would then go and try to make some order there. Have I paraphrased this correctly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: When you informed him that there were also paramilitary forces there and that he had already taken some steps and sent a dispatch to Serbia or maybe the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia - I don't know which it was at the time - because most of these paramilitary forces actually came from that part and he asked for them to be prevented from coming, crossing over from there. And this actually left you with the impression that he was prepared to do something about this.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mico Stanisic said that he had sent the -- this dispatch to a minister of the interior, the federal minister of the interior, in this sense that they should try and prevent the paramilitary forces from crossing over, and, yes, he did leave the impression that he was a man who was trying to solve this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to show the witness document number 192 -- 65 ter 192. Let's wait for that to come up. I see that -- all right. Now we have both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Here we are. On this first page, sir, Mr. Djokanovic, I just want you to see who actually prepared this document, this communication. It actually comes, this communication comes from the department for intelligence and security affairs, and they actually prepared a report on this particular subject that we were discussing; in other words, a report on paramilitary formations in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And as you can see on this first page, they're providing here the names of the groups, the paramilitary groups that were there, present. And then if you go further down the page you will also see how these groups are qualified by this department, and their intelligence service characterised most of these groups - not all of them - as criminal groups and that in some cases they had committed genocide. Can you see all of that? Are you following what I'm saying, and is this true, what I've just said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, I wanted to broach this topic and I've already used this document as an exhibit, but I would like to point you to page 3 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And perhaps Mr. Zecevic can find -- help me locate the English corresponding text. I think it might also be on page 3 or maybe a little further, page 4. There we have it. Just a moment, I'd like to find the portion that I would like to point out. In English it may be on the previous page -- no, no, no, just -- that's right. Let's just see the top of this page. That's fine. We found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: That's the first paragraph in the English version and it begins with the word "at." And then please read for us the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you can give me a hard copy of this, it would be easier for me to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you can just read from the -- from the screen.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At the moment there are about 60 paramilitary groups in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, totalling between 4 and 5.000 men. Here we list the most important."

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Please read the following line.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please just blow it up a bit. "A paramilitary unit with about 170 members" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we do have a hard copy, but I won't really insist. This is enough for my purposes, Your Honours. I won't need to use this document anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, if you could record -- to the particular paragraph in the original, it would be easier for the Registry to point that out to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we did point it out in the B/C/S version, that's the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I did see it, but I need a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in the English, that's the first paragraph beginning with "at" and then following on to the next paragraph. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But I can provide a hard copy if you like. Can you actually read it from the screen, or would you prefer to have a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really would prefer to have the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Here, please take a look at the second paragraph, and please don't read too fast so the interpreters can follow.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At the moment there are about 60 paramilitary groups in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, totalling between 4 and 5.000 men. Here we list the most important: "A paramilitary unit with about 170 members is located in the area of Zvornik, under the command of a certain self-styled Major Zuca ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I wanted to use. Now I need to get back my hard copy -- well, actually, Mr. Djokanovic, will you please turn to the next page where you can see that there is a portion relating to Teslic. Can you see that? Have you found that, where they've found a group of some 80 men; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, I just wanted to point out these statistics to you. I didn't really want you to assess them in any way. But my question was or is: Did you, Mr. Djokanovic, at this time when you visited Mr. Stanisic and when he told you these things about the problem, were you aware how widespread the use of paramilitary formations was at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to the meeting in early July, I believe, up to the 5th of July, one of those days?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as far as I can see, this document was prepared, this report was prepared toward the end of July, the 28th of July. Well, we did not discuss paramilitary units in specifics, how many men they number or what they are, we just discussed this in general terms. Mr. Stanisic said, "Mr. Djokanovic, we have major problems with paramilitary units."

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to point out what -- how big this problem was, and I just wanted to lay a foundation for my next question. Now, you would agree with me, Mr. Djokanovic, wouldn't you, that in addition to some honourable men, many of them were honourable men who came here to help the Serbian people and many of them were killed in fighting, but there was also a large number of them who actually took advantage of the status and the chaos there, the various uniforms that were used, the fear among the civilian population, and also the situation in the police station. So they actually took advantage of this and committed crimes; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and whatever they did, this will be lasting damage to the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me then that such units and such formations and armaments that they used called for the ministry to create a very strong and large enough special unit, train them, prepare them, and organise one operation after another, which also means that that would take a certain time before it could happen. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly how many of these paramilitary formations actually accepted to be submitted to the command of General Mladic, but many of them just continued doing whatever it was that they were -- they pleased. And of course the ministry had to prepare a special unit in order to fight these people, in order to have a show-down with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, all right, but let me just tell you that before this action in Zvornik was undertaken - and we've shown here -- we've tendered an exhibit to that effect - this intervention unit first intervened in Brcko and then in Zvornik, which is something of which you have knowledge. And then after Zvornik it also went to Rudo and Visegrad, and so on. So it took time to reach all those towns and places, and you would agree with me that this would call for major infrastructure to organise; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well -- Your Honour, I wish counsel would try and stop the witness when he sees me rising. At this point it's really too late, but I object because that question calls for speculation on the part of this witness. There's insufficient information in the question he put to him about all these towns they went to and how many paramilitaries they were dealing with, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I didn't specifically rule on Mr. Hannis's last objection, but the -- as with the last objection the -- it's a question, it seems to me, of formulating the question to the witness in a way which does not invite speculation and does not, as Mr. Hannis said on the previous occasion, assume facts that have yet to be established.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I told the witness that this unit before it intervened in Zvornik had also intervened in Brcko, and we have an exhibit that has already been admitted by this Trial Chamber. I didn't point this out to the witness, I didn't imply that the witness knew of this exhibit. This is Exhibit Number P339. But I assumed that this witness had knowledge about the engagement of this unit, and in any case he would have known about the -- their intervention in Zvornik because this is something that he was familiar with. And that's all I want to discuss with him, and then when other witnesses come we will discuss these other places. That's all I wanted to touch upon with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, at line 20 Mr. Cvijetic said: Your Honours, I told the witness blah. That is part of my problem. He is telling the witness many things, some of which there may have been evidence or a document about, but some which have not yet been. And he's testifying. That's my problem with what my learned friend is doing. And I would ask that he and you keep an eye on that, and I will try to stand up when I see it happening again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And, if I may add, Mr. Cvijetic, it would be useful if the witness could be interrupted from -- when you see an objection being taken by the other side. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, I will now put to you three documents in a row, all related to the topic that you focused on mostly during your evidence, and that is the topic of war crimes. I will give you these documents in the chronological order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 1D00-0509. Right. This is the document. Fortunately it's a one-page document and we just need to enlarge it enough so that the witness can see well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, please look at the heading. This document is dated the 5th of June, 1992. This is a letter from the Ministry of the Interior. It was drafted by the Assistant Minister For Prevention and Detection of Crime, Dobro Planojevic, you can see his signature.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that it's Dobro Planojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Would you please read it to yourself. It's quite brief. And then I will put some questions to you about it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have seen in the beginning is that Planojevic says that there is an increase in crime and war crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, and it says here in the middle that special attention is to be paid to uncovering perpetrators of war crimes, to documenting the criminal activities of individuals and groups, their apprehension, and ensuring that they are taken before responsible organs. Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And then towards the end, the penultimate sentence, it's longish, says: "Since in wartime you will encounter numerous obstacles in combatting crime and will on occasion be unable to take adequate measures, in such cases record all information in official notes for subsequent measures, necessary measures, i.e., criminal prosecution." Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, I will put the other two documents to you as well. But the problem that you were aware of is something that the Ministry of the Interior had also been aware of. And as a result, they sent an instruction to the CSBs on what needed to be done. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object the attempt to try to put this document in through this witness unless we have some further information that he knows who Mr. Planojevic was, he knows whether indeed this document was transmitted. It does not appear on its face that it was transmitted. There's no delivery information indicating it was actually sent. We don't know whether it was just a draft. I think this is not the appropriate witness to get this document in through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, before Mr. Cvijetic moved on from this document the question I was going to ask for my own edification, is, to whom -- is there any evidence to whom it's addressed? We know who it's purportedly signed by.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the heading it says to whom it was sent. Is that clear now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. What about Mr. Hannis's objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not intend to tender this document into evidence through this witness. I'm using these documents to show the witness what action was taken, what practical measures were taken by the ministry in order to prevent the problems that this witness pointed out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand this document is already a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. My colleague just told me that, yes, that's true. I can't mention the name of the witness through which it was introduced.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This makes it easier, Your Honours. I don't need to justify why I'm showing this document to the witness. It's already in evidence, but I've told you what my line of questioning was. 1D84. Your Honours, my next document, I have the number, is again the exhibit number, so it's already been admitted. Could we see P190. I think that's the right number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, may I comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Forgive me, but there was an objection so I couldn't ask you whether you knew anything about this. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Dobro Planojevic is a policeman, a professional policeman, and he drafted this document according to the rules that apply to professional policemen. But why did Dobro Planojevic disappear from the police infrastructure after this?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, he will come here as a witness so he can tell us about that himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have the document now? We do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, you can see from the heading the nature of this document, this is a letter and this is exhibit already admitted. And here we see that the problem that you informed Mr. Stanisic of and something that he's been informed of by Dobro Planojevic as well, we see here that he now in his turn informs Mr. Djeric of it and that he asks for political support for resolving this problem. Political support is the same term that you used. Is that clear from the text?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you agree with what I put to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. I will put to you now another exhibit, and we can see how the chronology evolved. The previous document was dated 18th of July and the next one is 19th of August, 1D63, again an exhibit in this case. All right, we have it now. Again, you'll have trouble reading this, since in the Serbian the text is on the first page and the second page is a form. Could we either enlarge it -- or rather, I'll give you a hard copy. That would be the best way to proceed. Now, before the break I will ask you to read this. And could we scroll down to the bottom of the page on the screen, please, and see the attachment that was sent with this letter of the minister. Yes, we have the attachment. You have seen this attachment too, haven't you, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: How did you understand this letter of Mr. Stanisic? Or would you agree with me that this is yet another step towards a practical implementation of the goal that we described, which was fighting against war crimes and war criminals?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this instruction and this form are indeed a practical implementation of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me just see the transcript. However, that is not enough. Practical steps needed to be taken as well, they needed to intervene wherever it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Practical steps were needed as well, but all of that needed to be prepared by politicians, otherwise there would have been no results without that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I will get to that, Mr. Djokanovic. I will get to the politicians and politics. I wanted to show you before that what Mr. Stanisic had done.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a different topic. Would you rather that I begin before the break? I have finished showing the documents to the witness, and I would like to turn to something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] We still have another 8 minutes to go before --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I thought that the break was at 10.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Djokanovic, you are aware, aren't you, that after all of these instructions, orders, documents with information and so on, Mr. Stanisic ordered that an operation be carried out in Zvornik, inter alia. I told you that we have evidence that an operation in Brcko preceded the one that you know of, so an operation was carried out in Zvornik in which 54 members of the Yellow Wasps were arrested, and they were arrested, prosecuted, expelled, and that this is how this group was broken down. Are you aware of this --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection. I think that assumes facts in evidence when he says 54 members were arrested, prosecuted, expelled. I don't think we have evidence that 54 members were prosecuted, et cetera. And this question is much more complicated and compound than it needs to be. The question could be, were you aware that there was an operation to arrest these men and Zvornik? And then we could go step by step. But Mr. Cvijetic tries to put too much into his question. And I think that makes it difficult for the witness, and it makes it difficult for you as the triers of fact to know exactly what he has answered yes to.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am relying on the statements that the witness gave to the OTP and on his evidence in Krajisnik. I know that this witness knows this. It's not by accident and without reference that I'm asking him this. And I will put reference to him in the next document that I will ask to be tendered. He doesn't need to know of the exact number of these members. I will prove that through the document that I have and the question that I put to him in the end: Do you know anything about this, are you aware of this? So the witness can say whether he is or he isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Aware of what, though, that 54 members were arrested? That 54 members were prosecuted? That 54 members were expelled? What? We have to break it down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Break up the question, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, do you know of things I that mentioned in my question, save for the figure? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that an operation was carried out. The special police of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska entered Zvornik, and then for a while after that they were stationed in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I think that you told us that part of that unit was present when this Assembly session was held and that the session was held without any incidents.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the November session?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think that they had their accommodation in the Drina hotel.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, but why don't you put to me the document that you showed me the other day about what the police investigation had shown -- carried out --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name of the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I was about to put that document to you. That was the next document I intended to put to you, and I wanted to broach that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Your Honours, I have several documents I want to put to this witness in a row, and I think it would be better if we did that after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the break now and return in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please look at document from the 65 ter list 296.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, this is document --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. We are not receiving the LiveNote on our computers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope I can begin now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, you had an opportunity to look at the document a little bit during this break. It's information drafted after the operation and the action against the Yellow Wasps on the 4th of August. And where you see what you see. I'm not going to read from it. You've seen when the monitoring of that group began, May/June 1992. The reason I wanted to show you this information actually is the last passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at page 3 of the Serbian version. Yes, it's the last page in both versions, so be it as it may. In the English can we please enlarge the last passage, the last passage, down there, down there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you please read that part.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So other than general crime for which this group was prosecuted, in the last paragraph it says that a person who perpetrated a war crime against Muslim civilians was placed at the disposal of the military police and the military forces for further processing in cooperation with the national security service of the MUP of Republika Srpska, which was gathering all of this information for that purpose. You would agree with me that perhaps this would be in the line of anticipated acts in the way that you would expect them to take place, don't you think so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: However, along this line of action, I have to show you the following document and that is 65 ter exhibit 2739.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. That is that document. Let's just check that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I'm not finding it in the list of documents that I was advised would be used with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was an e-mail about it this morning, 2739. You have it. There is an e-mail. You found it? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure. Can you give me the page number, the 1D page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I checked this morning. I think it's there. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, the next logical move, you would agree with me, would be the processing, the realisation of the information acquired by the police, and these would be criminal charges against this group. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. The reason I couldn't find it apparently is this already has an exhibit number in evidence as P322.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is the second document that I failed to secure, but it's easier than for me to explain why we're having it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, it's not yet time for you to answer. So the practical implementation would be in the processing, in the issuing of the criminal charges?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's answer was not heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at page 2 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Djokanovic, your answer was not registered when I asked you about the practical realisation you answered. Can you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was after the arrest, a logical step, criminal charges in terms of the prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we have clarification. Prosecution for which crimes? Car thefts or crimes against non-Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Again, the intervention in the transcript, it wasn't translated as the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat one more time, Mr. Djokanovic, for the third time. Please don't be mad.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the arrest of the members of the Yellow Wasps, the next logical step was to issue criminal charges from the Ministry of the Interior sent to the prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. In light of the objection by my learned friend the Prosecutor, can we please look at page 2 of the criminal charges. Ah, it's already there. I apologise. So after 11, paragraph 11, can we please scroll up. Scroll up if it's on that page, and I think that it is. And let's see if it's on that page, and I think it is, where it says "the individual named under number 9 ..." So that would be the second paragraph after the number 11 paragraph. Mr. Djokanovic, do you see it? Can you read it, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The individual named under 9 is currently remanded in custody at the Stepa Stepanovic military barracks in Bijeljina; the military organs decided that he be remanded into custody."

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can we go back now to see who is number 9.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Vuckovic, Dusko, a.k.a. Repic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to remind you of the last paragraph of the previous document where it is stated that the same was handed over to the military organs in cooperation with the security for -- service for national security. And this is actually what it practically says in this document, that this individual was remanded in custody.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to test your knowledge about jurisdiction and whether he was under the jurisdiction of the military organs because of the nature of the crime, it being a war crime. But I'm going to tell you, and I can even show you, that against him and his brother, criminal procedures were initiated for a war crime in the Republic of Serbia. I can show you --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please place on the monitor criminal charges for the war crime, and this is Exhibit 1D00-5858. Yes, that's it. Can we scroll it up a little bit? We haven't got it in the English version, but then when we do we can do the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, you can see here just who was charged. You can see that the Vuckovic brothers were charged, and then at the bottom when we scroll up the Serbian version we can see why. And it says: "On grounded suspicion that as co-perpetrators they perpetrated the criminal act of a war crime against a civilian person." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page. All right. We can enlarge that part and you can continue to read, sir. I don't know if you're familiar with the qualification of crimes and the law, but this is what I'm asserting it says here precisely, and so on and so forth. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have an objection to this. Yes, Mr. Cvijetic, is asserting several things, but the document speaks for itself. I don't know what comment we're trying to get from this witness that's going to advance your job. And if the document wants to be admitted, it can't come in through this witness. It's not -- he hasn't seen it before, he's not a military person, he can't explain it, he can't explain what the outcome of this was, if any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, what is your question of this witness, first of all?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm pursuing the line along the things that the witness is confirming for me, and I'm also following the line of the Prosecutor who's asking that I establish whether the Yellow Wasps were prosecuted for general crimes and for war crimes. I'm not asking him to know exactly the contents of these -- all right, well, let me tell the Prosecutor I'm not going to tender this report through this witness. I'm asking him. All right, now, I'm asking him whether he knows whether the Vuckovic brothers or Dusko Vuckovic, a.k.a. Repic, was prosecuted in Serbia for a war crime. Here, I'm going to ask him whether that was true or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. That -- I agree, that's an appropriate question. But to ask this witness to read something that's a document and say: Is that what it says? That's not a good use of our time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I think Mr. Cvijetic has taken your point on that, and he has formulated his question. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, there's nothing else left for you to do but to reply for this last question. I'm not going to deal with this last document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know from the media that the Vuckovic brothers were prosecuted in Serbia for war crimes committed in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djokanovic, now when we are pursuing, so to say, this line that you as a commissioner also pursued from initial information and if we parallelly follow this police line too, is this what you expected to be done by the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. You anticipated my next question because on Friday you finished your testimony with the words - I'm going to paraphrase as I cannot remember every word - but the policies did not accompany this action the way it should have done. Have I more or less paraphrased correctly what you said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to remind you of a small episode before I -- all right, I'm being told that I'm also going too fast. Yes, I'm being told that this thing about the policy is quite brief, but I'm going to actually show you documents where we will try to draw a broader answer to see what you meant to say. So I'm going to put questions to you where you can actually say in a little bit more detail what you wanted to say. I'm going to now put some questions to you in relation to an episode with Prime Minister Djeric. I think that you also discussed this with him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And you assert that he discretely, between the lines, conveyed a threat from the field, mostly from Zvornik, because you were talking a little bit too loudly about war crimes. Can you please explain in your own words so that I don't have to talk about it, and as briefly as possible so that you don't use up too much of my time.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The then-Prime Minister Djeric after a regional meeting held in Bijeljina, upon returning to Jahorina, told me that the local officer from Zvornik --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There is too much background noise, interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... said at that meeting in Bijeljina that he was charged by Alija Izetbegovic for war crimes and genocide in Bijeljina -- in Zvornik, and that this is also being repeated by the Serbian functioner -- functionary Djukanovic [as interpreted]. Branko Djeric said that after those words were spoken much had changed as far as I was concerned and that I needed to pay attention to my security. It says Djukanovic here, but actually it is Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My microphone was off, so I have to repeat the question. Did he tell you specifically who it was who voiced this? You said that he said, "You have greetings from Zvornik." Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, explain it, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said, "You have greetings from Zvornik." I thought that this was really well meant, these greetings, and I said to him, "Well, yes, I used to work there as a doctor and I know those people." However, a few days later Branko Djeric came to see me at the Presidency in Pale, and what he said earlier was on Jahorina. So he came and he told me in more detail about the meeting in Bijeljina, and he told me literally the following. "Dragan [as interpreted] Grujic said in Bijeljina that Alija Izetbegovic had accused him of the crimes in Zvornik, but he was also accused by a Serb official, Djokanovic. And then Djeric told me, with the best of intentions, that after such words had been said and spoken I should take certain steps in order to ensure my own safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name of the person who -- the name did not enter -- the right name did not enter the transcript. So could you please repeat the name.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was Branko Grujic, who told -- who said in this meeting in Bijeljina that he had been accused of war crimes by the -- by Alija Izetbegovic, but also by a Serbian official Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Could you tell us other than a fear for your safety, did you observe that he, too, had certain concerns about his own safety, Mr. Djeric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. We were discussing the re-shuffling of government, and after this conversation that we had, he mentioned or offered me to be a member of his government.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, within the context of your -- of what you've told us about the lack of political support, I will now put to you the document that had already been used by the Prosecutor, that's 65 ter 933. And while we're looking for the document, let me just say that this is a -- this document relates to the meeting of the 23rd and 24th of November, 1992. You said that you attend -- you had attended this session; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Please bear with me a moment. Let us just find that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have page 18 and then 19 in the B/C/S version, and in English that will be on page 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, I think that's one I referred to this morning, and we've marked it as P400, but I've since discovered that I think it already had a P number of 202. So I'm not sure how we fix that, but it does have a P number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We're advised that the previous number has fallen away so the number can remain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank my learned colleague for following all these numbers, exhibit numbers. Obviously I'm not as good with the numbers as he is, and I may have or might have brought additional confusion with a third number that I would come up with. I think we have the right page -- or rather, no. The B/C/S version I need page 18, in other words the next page. Just one page. We do have the right page in the English. Could we just scroll up or down the Serbian version, the remarks by Biljana Plavsic. This is where it begins, and in English we can see that it's a longer portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, would you please just read the introductory remarks by Mrs. Plavsic, and once you have done that could we please scroll it to the next page. So that would be on page 19 in the Serbian version. We don't have it yet. I don't know what is going on. So let's just zoom in on the first paragraph. Mr. Djokanovic, would you read the entire paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read it, and I have to say I remember her remarks almost in their entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. What I will do now is paraphrase. I don't want to read through because we can all read what it says there. But let me paraphrase. You would agree with me that Mrs. Plavsic is actually defending herself here, defending against the rumours that she was the one who brought these volunteers, as it were, these paramilitary units. She -- her defence amounts to her publicly acknowledging this; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
